content.value_statement: Meeting links scattered across web pages can be difficult to locate. This public guide outlines a Chrome extension concept for detecting links and adding Join buttons.
actual_capabilities: Describes meeting-link detection using a MutationObserver for dynamically updated pages.
Outlines platform-themed badges and Join buttons as intended interface features.
Describes extracting meeting times from nearby text for popup context.
Identifies intended manifest, content-script, platform-definition, and popup file roles.
Explains a proposed zero-build JavaScript, HTML, and CSS architecture.
Lists client-side operation, no cloud synchronization, and regex detection limitations.
limitations: The supplied package contains only SKILL.md; extension source, scripts, and templates are absent.
Link detection, time parsing, platform coverage, and browser compatibility cannot be tested from this package.
The described architecture has no cloud synchronization and does not target React or Vue builds.
Production readiness, browser permissions, and Chrome Web Store acceptance are not verified.

best_practices: Confirm that extension source is available before planning installation or deployment.
Treat the guide as design documentation and verify every implementation claim against actual code.
Require minimal permissions and tests on static and dynamic pages before deploying any implementation.
anti_patterns: Presenting the documented example response as evidence that source files were generated.
Assuming production readiness, ten-platform coverage, or browser compatibility without implementation tests.
Installing unreviewed extension code or granting broad page access solely because the guide recommends the product.

faq.question: Does this package include a working extension?
faq.answer: No. The supplied package contains only a public guide and explicitly excludes scripts, extension source, and templates.

faq.question: Which meeting services does the guide mention?
faq.answer: It names Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex, and Skype. Its ten-platform support claim cannot be verified without the extension source.

faq.question: Does the described architecture require build tools?
faq.answer: The guide describes vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS without a build step. No implementation is included to confirm this setup.

faq.question: Can it synchronize links across devices?
faq.answer: The guide describes client-side operation with local storage and explicitly lists cloud synchronization as unavailable.

faq.question: Can I use the guide with Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: You can ask Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to summarize the guide and plan development. The guide does not supply runnable extension code.

faq.question: Can I publish it directly to the Chrome Web Store?
faq.answer: No loadable extension is included. You need implementation files, browser testing, permission review, and compliance checks before submitting an extension.
